claim: For the gain-one coherent-state teleportation fidelity of Gábris and Agarwal's pair-coherent resource, with \(\zeta\ge0\), the published double series sums exactly to \[\mathcal F_{\rm av}(\zeta,1)=\frac{e^{\zeta}I_0(\zeta)}{2I_0(2\zeta)}.\] Moreover, as \(\zeta\to\infty\), \[\mathcal F_{\rm av}(\zeta,1)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(1+\frac1{16\zeta}+\frac{25}{512\zeta^2}+O(\zeta^{-3})\right).\] Hence the large-intensity fidelity tends exactly to \(1/\sqrt2\) from above; in particular it eventually exceeds \(2/3\), sharpening the source's qualitative statement that the gain-one fidelity approaches a limit above \(1/2\).
integrity: The exact reduction is proved by regrouping an absolutely convergent nonnegative series, Vandermonde identity, and an Euler-integral representation. The asymptotic uses the standard large-argument expansion of \\(I_0\\). Numerical replay is supplementary only.
scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to the Gábris--Agarwal coherent-state protocol at fixed gain \\(g=1\\). It does not prove uniqueness of the finite-\\(\\zeta\\) maximum, optimize over gain, or cover decohered or modified pair-coherent resources.
title: Closed Bessel form and exact high-intensity limit for gain-one pair-coherent teleportation
